claim_1.claim: Computational model analysis of immunological and gene expression profiles from 91 healthy donors vaccinated during the fall of 2008, using a combination of nuclear norm and Elastic net methods, showed that yCMV− and yCMV+ subjects could be separated by regression coefficients used to separate the classes, with 79% accuracy compared to the comparator population.

sources.quote: The accuracy of the computational models to distinguish yCMV− vs yCMV+ and yCMV− vs oCMV− were 79% and 91.7%, respectively (Table S2), indicating that aging has a more profound effect on the immune system than latent CMV.

Figure 1 Different immunological profiles in aging versus CMV seropositivityThe contribution of age and CMV to immunological and gene expression profiles was estimated by a combination of nuclear norm and the Elastic net methods (see Methods). The magnitude of the regression coefficients used to separate the classes yCMV− and oCMV− (CMV-independent age effect) or yCMV− and yCMV+ (age-independent CMV effect) are shown in light and dark grey bars, respectively.

claim_3.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMC from 91 healthy donors vaccinated during the fall of 2008, using the regression coefficients from a combination of nuclear norm and Elastic net methods, showed that CD8+ effector memory (TEM) and CD8+ CD28− cell frequencies overlapped between the yCMV− versus oCMV− and yCMV− versus yCMV+ classification tasks.

sources.quote: The only exceptions to this were the CD8+ effector memory (TEM) and CD8+ CD28− cell frequencies, both being positively correlated with age and CMV.
Only two parameters, the frequency of CD8+ CD28− and CD8+ TEM cells, overlapped between these classification tasks.

claim_4.claim: Analysis of immunological and gene expression profiles from 91 healthy donors vaccinated during the fall of 2008, using a combination of nuclear norm and Elastic net methods, showed that 16 of 23 parameters used to separate the yCMV− and oCMV− classes were down-regulated in aging.

sources.quote: Strikingly, while expression of most parameters (71%, 17/24) decreased with age, the majority (88%, 14/16) increased with CMV seropositivity in young individuals (Fig. 1 and Table S2), indicating an overall down-regulation of the immune response and associated parameters during aging and an up-regulation of several components of the immune system in young subjects with latent CMV.

14/16 (87.5%) of the parameters used to separate the yCMV− from yCMV+ classes were up-regulated in CMV, in contrast, the majority of parameters used to separate the yCMV− from oCMV− classes (16/23, 69.5%) were down-regulated in aging.

claim_6.claim: Hemagglutination inhibition assay analysis of serum from 91 healthy donors vaccinated with seasonal trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine across the first and second study years, using geometric mean titer delta post- minus pre-vaccination, showed that the antibody response to IIV was lower with age compared to younger subjects.

sources.quote: We computed the pre- and post-vaccine geometric mean titer (GMT) for all three strains in the vaccine and calculated a response score as the delta post- minus pre-GMT. As expected, a negative effect of age was observed in the antibody response to IIV (P < 0.0001) (Fig. 2a).

claim_7.claim: Hemagglutination inhibition assay analysis of serum from young vaccinated subjects in the first study year (20-30 years old), using geometric mean titer delta post- minus pre-vaccination, showed that the antibody response was higher in yCMV+ compared to yCMV− subjects.

sources.quote: Surprisingly, in the yCMV+ group the antibody response was higher than in yCMV− subjects (P = 0.03) (Fig. 2a).
A higher response is observed in yCMV+ compared to yCMV− in the first (a) and second (b) year, as well as in an independent validation study conducted during the 2010-2011 influenza season (c).

claim_8.claim: Hemagglutination inhibition assay analysis of serum from older vaccinated subjects in the first study year (60->89 years old), using geometric mean titer delta post- minus pre-vaccination, showed that CMV-related differences in antibody response were not significant compared to oCMV− subjects.

sources.quote: These CMV-related differences were not significant in the older cohort (Fig. 2a and b).
No significant differences were observed between oCMV− and oCMV+.

claim_9.claim: Hemagglutination inhibition assay analysis of serum from the 77 individuals who returned one year later during the 2009-2010 influenza season, including young subjects aged 22-32 years, using geometric mean titer delta post- minus pre-vaccination, showed that CMV had a positive effect on antibody response in the young compared to young CMV-seronegative subjects.

sources.quote: A similar positive effect of CMV in the young (P = 0.04) but not the older cohort was observed in the 77 individuals who returned one year later during the 2009-2010 influenza season (Fig. 2b).
A higher response is observed in yCMV+ compared to yCMV− in the first (a) and second (b) year, as well as in an independent validation study conducted during the 2010-2011 influenza season (c).

claim_10.claim: Hemagglutination inhibition assay analysis of serum from the 77 individuals who returned one year later during the 2009-2010 influenza season, including older subjects aged 62->89 years, using geometric mean titer delta post- minus pre-vaccination, showed that the CMV effect on antibody response was not significant in the older cohort compared to oCMV− subjects.

sources.quote: A similar positive effect of CMV in the young (P = 0.04) but not the older cohort was observed in the 77 individuals who returned one year later during the 2009-2010 influenza season (Fig. 2b).
No significant differences were observed between oCMV− and oCMV+.

claim_11.claim: Hemagglutination inhibition assay analysis of serum from an independent cohort of 37 young individuals recruited during the 2010-2011 influenza season (19-44 years old), using geometric mean titer delta post- minus pre-vaccination, showed that CMV had a positive effect on antibody response in the young compared to young CMV-seronegative subjects.

sources.quote: In addition, these findings were validated in an independent cohort of 37 young individuals recruited during the 2010-2011 influenza season (P = 0.017) (Fig. 2c).
A higher response is observed in yCMV+ compared to yCMV− in the first (a) and second (b) year, as well as in an independent validation study conducted during the 2010-2011 influenza season (c).

claim_12.claim: Plaque assay analysis of lungs from groups of C57BL/6 mice mock infected or infected with 4×10^4 PFU MCMV Smith strain i.p. and challenged with 10^6 EID50 of IAV ×31 i.n. 5 weeks later, showed reduced influenza viral titers in IAV+ MCMV+ mice compared to IAV+ MCMV− mice at day 7 after IAV infection.

sources.quote: Both in early and established latency, we observed better protection against influenza in the MCMV-infected (IAV+ MCMV+) versus the mock-infected (IAV+ MCMV−) mice at day 7 after IAV challenge as seen by the reduced influenza viral titers in the lungs (Fig. 3a and b).

Figure 3 Reduced viral titer and enhanced IAV-specific CD8+ T cell responses in early and established but not long-standing MCMV latencyGroups of C57BL/6 mice were mock infected or infected with 4×104 PFU MCMV Smith strain i.p. and challenged with 106 EID50 of IAV ×31 i.n. 5 weeks (early latency) (a and d), 12 weeks (established latency) (b and e) or 9 months (long-standing latency) later (c and f). Seven days after IAV infection, influenza viral titer was determined (upper panel) and IAV-specific T cells were enumerated from the BAL of IAV+ MCMV− (MCMV−) or IAV+ MCMV+ (MCMV+) mice by tetramer staining for NP, PA and PB1-specific responses. Data are representative of three independent experiments with 4-6 mice per group in each experiment. Significance was determined by t-test for viral titer and using the Fisher’s combined probability test for comparison of specific T cell responses.

claim_15.claim: Tetramer staining analysis of BAL from groups of C57BL/6 mice mock infected or infected with 4×10^4 PFU MCMV Smith strain i.p. and challenged with 10^6 EID50 of IAV ×31 i.n. 5 weeks later, showed higher IAV-specific T cell responses against NP, PA and PB1 in IAV+ MCMV+ mice compared to IAV+ MCMV− mice at day 7 after IAV infection.

sources.quote: Consistent with this observation, the influenza-specific CD8+ T cell responses against the three major influenza epitopes (DbPA224--233 (PA), KbPB1703-711 (PB1), and DbNP366-374 (NP)) in BAL cells were higher in animals with early and established latency, but not after long-standing latency compared with the mock-infected group (Fig. 3d-f).

claim_18.claim: Plaque assay analysis of lung homogenates from IFN-γ-deficient or wild-type C57BL/6 co-infected mice challenged 5-6 weeks after MCMV infection with influenza A virus, showed higher influenza viral titers in IFN-γ-deficient IAV+ MCMV+ mice compared to wild-type IAV+ MCMV+ mice at day 7 after IAV infection.

sources.quote: To test this, we monitored the influenza viral titer in the lungs and also the number of influenza-specific CD8+ T cells in IFN-γ knock-out (KO) or control mice challenged with IAV at 5 weeks after MCMV infection, as described earlier. Significantly higher viral titers and lower influenza-specific responses were observed in the IFN-γ KO compared to control mice (Fig 4a and b), demonstrating that IFN-γ is essential for the MCMV-induced cross-protection against influenza in young mice during early MCMV latency and probably also contributes to this effect directly through its antiviral activity.

Figure 4 The effect of MCMV on cross-protection against influenza is IFN-γ-mediatedGroups of C57BL/6 mice or IFN-γ-deficient mice (on the C57BL/6 background) were mock infected or infected with 4×104 PFU MCMV Smith strain i.p. and challenged 5-6 weeks later with 106 EID50 of IAV x31 i.n. (a) IAV lung viral titers from control (wild-type, WT) or IFN-γ-deficient co-infected (IAV+ MCMV+) mice were determined at day 7 after IAV infection in early MCMV latency (>5 weeks).

claim_19.claim: Tetramer staining analysis of BAL from wild-type or IFN-γ-deficient C57BL/6 MCMV and IAV co-infected mice challenged 5-6 weeks after MCMV infection with influenza A virus, showed lower influenza-specific CD8+ T cell responses against NP, PA and PB1 in IFN-γ-deficient mice compared to wild-type mice at day 7 after IAV infection.

sources.quote: To test this, we monitored the influenza viral titer in the lungs and also the number of influenza-specific CD8+ T cells in IFN-γ knock-out (KO) or control mice challenged with IAV at 5 weeks after MCMV infection, as described earlier. Significantly higher viral titers and lower influenza-specific responses were observed in the IFN-γ KO compared to control mice (Fig 4a and b), demonstrating that IFN-γ is essential for the MCMV-induced cross-protection against influenza in young mice during early MCMV latency and probably also contributes to this effect directly through its antiviral activity.

(b) IAV-specific CD8+ T cells were enumerated from the BAL of WT and IFN-γ-deficient MCMV and IAV co-infected mice by tetramer staining for NP, PA and PB1-specific responses, 7 days after IAV infection. Significance was determined by t-test. Data are representative of two independent experiments with 3-5 mice per group. Significance was determined by t-test for viral titer and using the Fisher’s combined probability test for comparison of specific T cell responses.
